story: In 1788, astronomer William Herschel discovered NGC 4449, an irregular dwarf galaxy in the constellation Canes Venatici located roughly 10 to 13 million light-years away. Also known as Caldwell 21, this small galaxy belongs to a local group of galaxies in Canes Venatici. Despite its small dwarf size, NGC 4449 is undergoing a magnificent cosmic phenomenon known as a starburst, producing brand new stars at an extraordinarily high rate. Astronomers believe this intense wave of star formation was spurred by gravitational interactions with nearby neighboring galaxies. Images of NGC 4449 illuminate vibrant young massive stars and dusty pink glowing regions that mark active stellar nurseries where massive new stars flare into existence.
angle: NGC 4449 is a dwarf galaxy undergoing such a hyper-intense starburst—spurred by galactic collisions—that dusty pink star nurseries glow throughout its entire structure.
